transcript:
Header: 2026-11-11 10:00 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Claire D, Miguel S, Jasmine L (Redwood) — Arjun, Sofia, Tom, Priya (Novapay)

00:00 Claire Dunn: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the latest throughput numbers and tuning ideas. quick check — prod profile from Novapay, did you get that in?
00:12 Arjun Mehta: yeah we uploaded a rough histogram, sent to the shared drive, it's in the sheet, sorry there's a couple of edits after the spike window.
00:20 Miguel Santos: ok good. um quick status: last week we bumped the continuous batching window to 20ms and enabled dynamic batch cap. we saw tokens/sec go up ~28% but tail latency at p99 increased during the burst test.
00:35 Tom Reynolds: that jives with what we saw. p50 stayed fine but p99 jumped from 420ms to about 1.1s when concurrency hit 128.
00:48 Claire Dunn: right so tradeoff: bigger batch means better throughput economics but risks queueing and head-of-line latency. we're trying to find the knee.
00:59 Sofia Alvarez: can you clarify how queueing is implemented currently? is it first-in-first-out or some priority for small requests?
01:06 Miguel Santos: currently FIFO with a small heuristic that tries to coalesce requests by prompt length to maximize packing. there's no size-priority preemptive scheduling yet — that's on the roadmap.
01:20 Priya Kapoor: and the cache hit rates — prefix cache, KV cache — we had a lot of cold misses in the spike test, I think because sessions were new. that also pushed more tokens through.
01:34 Miguel Santos: yep prefix cache hit was around 42% during the burst, down from 78% on steady traffic. those misses add both compute and latency. we recommended sticky session hashing to improve locality.
01:47 Arjun Mehta: sticky sessions is doable but our load balancer routing is a bit more complex because we have regional failover. will need to coordinate with infra.
01:58 Claire Dunn: for today's run we wanted to validate two knobs: one, set a concurrency target (e.g., 64 vs 128) and two, tune continuous batching parameters (window ms and batch cap). Miguel has a proposal.
02:12 Miguel Santos: proposal A: concurrency target 64, batch cap 128, batch window 12ms, enable prefix sticky routing where possible. proposal B: concurrency 96, batch cap 64, window 20ms as a compromise for latency.
02:26 Tom Reynolds: can you explain batch cap again? I thought cap was per GPU or per model shard?
02:33 Miguel Santos: it's an upper bound on how many tokens/requests we will group before dispatch. it's per worker process. if you set cap too high you get long wait before dispatch. cap relates to latency tail.
02:47 Priya Kapoor: curious about backpressure — when queue fills, do requests get rejected or queued with a timeout?
02:54 Miguel Santos: currently we queue up to a soft limit and then start 429-retries for excess — but we also have an adaptive shedding policy that prefers short requests to maintain p50. in practice that behavior needs tuning for your traffic mix.
03:12 Arjun Mehta: what's the recommended retry strategy? we don't want upstream clients hammering endpoints on 429s and making cascading retries.
03:20 Claire Dunn: recommended pattern: exponential backoff with jitter plus a small max retry (2-3), and prefer client-side rate limiting based on returned headers. we'll send a guidance doc.
03:32 Miguel Santos: also, consider a leaky-bucket at the edge to smooth arrival bursts. that paired with sticky sessions and a slightly lower concurrency target should reduce p99.
03:46 Tom Reynolds: numbers — can you share the exact throughput delta for proposal A vs B?
03:50 Miguel Santos: from our lab runs: baseline (window 20ms, cap 64, concurrency 96) = ~18k tokens/s; proposal A (12ms, cap 128, concurrency 64) = ~22.8k tokens/s but p99 went to ~1.05s under burst; proposal B (20ms, cap 64, concurrency 96) = ~19.6k tokens/s with p99 ~620ms.
04:14 Priya Kapoor: ok so A is best raw throughput but worst tail. B is middle ground.
04:20 Claire Dunn: what are your SLA targets for p99 and for cost? what matters most?
04:25 Arjun Mehta: we care about p99 under 700ms for user-facing flows, but for back-office async tasks we can tolerate more. most critical is checkout path — it needs p99 < 800ms. cost target is to keep token cost within 15% of our current inference budget.
04:41 Claire Dunn: given that, B seems safer. we can also do hybrid: route checkout traffic to a lower-concurrency, lower-batch pool and background predictions to the high-throughput pool.
04:52 Tom Reynolds: how easy is multi-pool routing? can we do that in the POC?
04:56 Miguel Santos: yes we can create per-route policies, it's already supported — just need labeling on your requests so router knows the route. can demo in the perf window.
05:08 Jasmine Lee: quick note on metrics you'll get: token/sec by model, p50/p90/p99 latencies, batch sizes over time, prefix cache hit ratio, and queue depth histogram. we'll include those in the spreadsheet.
05:19 Arjun Mehta: what's the expected infra commitment for the dedicated perf run? we prefer a small dedicated pool for the test rather than shared infra.
05:27 Miguel Santos: for a 2-hour perf run at your desired load with headroom, we recommend 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool; if you want to emulate peak bursts use 6. we'll provide configs.
05:41 Priya Kapoor: about KMS and logs for the dedicated run — need to ensure logs don't leave our VPC. is that supported?
05:48 Claire Dunn: yes for Private/Dedicated we can keep logs in your VPC and integrate with your KMS. we'll send the security checklist and SOC 2 artifacts.
05:57 Arjun Mehta: perfect. any blockers on our side? we need to run an internal change for sticky sessions and label the checkout route.
06:05 Tom Reynolds: I'll create a ticket, assign to SRE. expected ETA 2 days.
06:10 Claire Dunn: recap and next steps: Claire — send spreadsheet and config recommendations; Miguel — run bench and upload logs; Novapay — prod profile + enable routing label + provision subnet for perf window. schedule perf for 2026-11-20.
06:25 Arjun Mehta: sounds good. thanks all.

[end transcript]
